The source recommends confirming whether the PIT-101 low-pressure alarm is active in the control room and activating it if necessary. Synthetic decision-model assumptions: the fixed cost is in arbitrary normalized units, not a source-derived price. The stated reliability is experimentally stipulated, not a source-derived performance estimate. The proposed activation applies when the check identifies a need; the worksheet does not establish that an active alarm must be newly installed. A demand means a low-pressure alarm demand after the proposed check and any necessary activation. Success means delivery of the intended low-pressure indication in the control room. parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: HAZOP basis: the design intent is to keep the crude input line and separator V-001 at their intended operating pressure, and the deviation is Low pressure (CASE-02). The packet does not detail causes or consequence mechanisms. The source ranks the scenario as frequency B, severity I, Low risk, and lists no existing safeguard (CASE-03). Its recommendation is to confirm whether the PIT-101 low-pressure alarm is active in the control room and activate it if necessary. Reliability interpretation: unavailability on 5 of 100 demands is numerically identical to successful indication on 95 of 100 demands (95%). Over the next 100 eligible demands this means about 95 delivered indications and about 5 missed, compared with no listed safeguard today. Decision: the Low risk ranking does not justify elaborate protection. However, this action is a proportionate, source-recommended check-and-activate step on the PIT-101 alarm named in the worksheet. It closes an identified safeguard gap and improves operator awareness of the deviation. The 20-unit fixed cost is normalized and is not shown to breach any stated constraint. Management should therefore not reject the recommendation; the canonical recommendation is approve. The alarm should be credited only as an indication measure. Its 95% delivery does not quantify accident prevention or eliminate residual risk. The outcome of the confirmation check should be documented so the alarm status is verifiable. Because engineering facts and cost are identical across frames (CASE-04), the decision rests on the numerical reliability, not the loss-framed wording.
